exemplars.title: GeoVisA11y: An AI-based Geovisualization Question-Answering System for Screen-Reader Users
exemplars.why: GeoVisA11y preserves geographic topology as addressable state nodes and uses a persistent focus cursor with discrete cardinal commands, enabling screen-reader users to traverse the map rather than receive a flattened description.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It is stronger than SeeChart because its direction-sensitive adjacency graph demonstrates genuinely structural navigation, whereas SeeChart only establishes linear movement between charts.

exemplars.title: SeeChart: Enabling Accessible Visualizations Through Interactive Natural Language Interface For People with Visual Impairments
exemplars.why: SeeChart reconstructs multiple charts as addressable items and maintains a cursor that users advance or reverse with dedicated N/P commands in a screen-reader-oriented interface.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It is stronger than ImageExplorer because the evidence explicitly establishes discrete traversal and persistent position between nodes, while ImageExplorer only demonstrates entering a nested layer.

exemplars.title: ImageExplorer: Multi-Layered Touch Exploration to Encourage Skepticism Towards Imperfect AI-Generated Image Captions
exemplars.why: ImageExplorer parses an image into nested object and sub-object nodes and supplies a discrete double-tap command for moving into the hierarchy, giving it part of the pattern's graph-traversal structure.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: It edges out AskEase because its object hierarchy and into-layer transition preserve non-linear structure, whereas AskEase is ordinary pagination through an already linear chat history.

notes: I departed from the consensus by selecting rid 832 instead of the higher-scoring rid 5950. AskEase conflicts with the definition's explicit rejection of flattening into a single linear sequence, while ImageExplorer at least exposes hierarchical nodes and an into command. No individual score adjustment exceeds 0.3. All three selections have evidence limitations: GeoVisA11y does not explicitly quote the spoken response or orientation announcement; SeeChart's quote is truncated and establishes neither within-chart traversal nor an announced position; ImageExplorer is a borderline third exemplar because the supplied evidence emphasizes visible boundaries and does not establish a persistent cursor, nonvisual node rendering, or orientation cues. Only four of the stated seven candidates were supplied, so the selection is necessarily limited to those records.
